item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 9
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 9. 7/10. This episode included

  1. Maki was accepted to join the Christmas party
  2. Maki talked with his mother about the truth about their living expenses
  3. Maki visited Umi's house

The main part of this episode was how Maki reacted to seeing Umi's family while they had a normal conversation like a family does, and that reminded Maki of his family's past Maki's past with his family was short, simple, but still sad enough for a character of a slice-of-life anime. And his reaction was quiet, but he couldn't stop crying — exactly like his character, who cared about others and who didn't attack or blame others. And Umi was, well, maybe the ideal girl who chased him regardless of whether he ran away or not, and calmed him down and stayed with him. It was well drawn that she thanked him in earlier episodes that he meant a lot to her, and also, Maki didn't recognize it. From Maki's perspective, she was the first friend who was nice to him and got along with him, so probably he thought it was nothing special. Now, come to think of it, he didn't have any friends because he moved schools from time to time, so his family was everything to him, and I can imagine the divorce of his parents hurt a lot.

The other parts are minor. Early in this episode, Amami was unwilling to see Umi's brother, but this episode didn't show how creepy his behavior was. Only Umi described what his behavior was like. Umi's father was very tall, a head taller than Maki, but like Maki, he was kind, and Umi's mother always led the conversation. It wasn't such a shock that Maki's mother didn't say anything about the living expenses she was trying to earn without using the money she got from Maki's father. I still don't exactly know what happened between them, but she might be kinda stubborn, or hasn't forgiven what he did. In the scene where Umi caught Maki after he ran away, the background was someone's house decorated cleanly and brightly for Christmas, so that brightness and beauty made it clear they were moving forward in a good way. Before he ran away, it was a plain street without good lighting, so at that time, it showed how depressed Maki was.

There were a few things wrong about the nitty-gritty. Maki started running away and Umi was trying to catch up. But they were just eating dinner and went out suddenly, so running in such a condition should hurt them and it was hard to run. They were emotional and they didn't care about that, though. Also, when Umi was trying to make Maki sleep in her lap, the camera was from Maki's eyeline. But it looked at Umi, though he was obviously looking in a different direction, so I wanted the previous cut to be consistent.

Well, anyway, what I wanted to say was they were a match made in heaven, even compared to any other anime. I don't know what Maki will do in the next episode, but he'll probably invite his parents to the school's Christmas party and try to get them to work out their arguments. And they would start living together, but I guess it won't happen.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 8
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 8. 5/10. This episode included

  1. Study group at Maki's home for the next exam
  2. Dinner with Maki's father and met Nitta afterward
  3. Talked to Umi

Well, if you want a romantic relationship between Maki and Umi, then this episode is great. The early part of this episode was especially good — their interaction while they studied with Amami and Seki together. Another interesting part was Amami's personal preference was similar to Maki's, and she wanted to date someone like him. Well, maybe she just had a big appetite and a sweet tooth, and wanted to eat them. Umi heard these things and worried about Maki, and said that she had put up with it in the past when Amami took her friends — Honoka, and one more whose name I forgot. But she definitely couldn't. If she had been able to, she wouldn't have changed high schools in the first place. So she worried but at the same time, her sadness faded because of Maki.

This episode also showed who was smart, and Amami and Seki weren't as smart as Umi and Maki. So, Amami's other weakness was actually studying.

In terms of the dinner scene with Maki's dad, well, I kinda understood and kinda felt weird when Maki was angry. He was angry because his dad loved another woman but found out he loved her after he had divorced Maki's mom. He also saw that his mom looked wiped out so from that kindness, it made sense that he couldn't forgive. At the same time, they were divorced, so even if he was their son, didn't it make sense?

Well, and Nitta somehow played a role in calming Maki down. She's been a kinda convenient character so far. Probably she also talked to Umi and Umi set up the dinner with her family and Maki next time.

Well, nothing too special. In the next episode, Maki will see a normal family life and then, I'm not sure what's going to happen. Maybe he will get mad and argue with Umi, or the opposite and relieved with their life? Let's see.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 7
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 7. 5/10.

  • Story and characters: 3/5
  • Design and animation: 3/5
  • Voices and audios: 3/5

This episode started with:

  1. The threesome went shopping and ran into Maki's dad
  2. The next day, Umi and Maki went on a date and ran into his dad again
  3. Maki talked to his mom after the date

So, in terms of rom-com, this episode is gold. It's clear Umi almost always led their date and she was trying to get closer to him, and their opinions sometimes lined up. This was her first or second date, so thinking about it, she prepared a lot for the date — finding Maki's clothes, preparing her own clothes, finding a theater, and a few restaurants, too. I wanted to see more of the karaoke scene but the singing was cut.

Even though this episode showed a good side of rom-com, that scene was the moment before Maki had his work cut out for him, and that's how the story went. I shouldn't say anything whether Maki's dad was bad or not until next episode. That depends on whether he had dated anyone before his divorce. At least, that guy paid for Maki's minor living expenses so seems okay.

In terms of animation, it seems the drawing isn't good when a character is drawn from the side, though. Also, there was a scene where the camera was placed low, under the table. When Umi came to Maki's room, there were several shots showing her girly outfit from different angles.

I didn't notice anything specific to audios stuff.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 6
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 6. 6/10.

  • Story and characters: 4/5
  • Design and animation: 3/5
  • Voices and audios: 3/5

The episode started basically with:

  1. The dream about the time when Maki cried out to his dad.
  2. Planning for this Christmas Eve.
  3. Seki's confession to Amami.
  4. Maki's preparation for his next date with Umi.

In this episode, finally, Maki's dad was mentioned, and unlike some MCs in other anime, he had a reason why he didn't live with his dad. And that seemed to be his trauma or something as he dreamed about it. And it also influenced his personality, and he wanted to be a better guy for Umi before officially dating her. At least we know why his character was something like this.

Nitta and Seki finally talked a lot in this episode, and they are also animated in the opening. I am still unsure about Nitta's personality honestly, but Seki was a baseball jock and takes action quickly rather than thinking too much, and confessed to Amami. He didn't really talk to her so obviously she turned him down, and because of that, he and Maki became friends. So, I think this person will get along with Maki a lot later.

People knew about Maki and Umi's relationship, but some people didn't know they weren't dating. Because Seki mentioned that Umi got popular in those days, as I guessed in the previous episode, another hot guy will show up and become Maki's rival in a later episode. Well, or rather, it's more accurate to say they were already dating and just didn't admit it. It was ironic that Umi was more like a lead all the time but she was blushing when she talked about Maki with someone else.

There were a lot of low-angle shots showing legs a couple of times in this episode. The first was while Umi and Maki were talking in his room, and it was like, why? Heads or the upper body can show the slight behaviors of each character better than the movement of the lower body while they were sitting. It also happened while they were walking in a shopping mall. This can show the movements and also cut animation and drawing costs, so maybe this was fine.

For the next episode, I wasn't sure how his dad will be involved in the story. Maybe Maki couldn't go to the date and Umi figured it out, but then, what? I cannot guess. Either his mom will find a new man or they will get back together might be the best one but I don't know what is a good one.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 5
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 5. 9/10.

  • Story and characters: 5/5
  • Design and animation: 3/5
  • Voices and audios: 3/5

The earlier part of this episode was that Umi started talking about her past and the reactions there, and then Umi and Maki talked in a classroom. The later part was that Umi talked with Amami on the roof with Maki again, and then they hung out in Maki's room before they called it a day. I didn't expect this episode was still on the school festival day, and I thought it had finished in the previous episode, but I was wrong.

I like the overall story in the episode. This episode showed how Umi really felt about Amami, and it wasn't very simple. It was love and hate. I also wondered why she talked with the other 2 girls, but her past explained it well, and that was also sad but at the same time a pretty natural thing, too, because human relationships can change over time. And that explained why Umi and Amami at least went to that high school, instead of moving up to the high school attached to their middle school, which they could have entered without taking an exam. Although, I wasn't sure why other girls also followed them and entered the same school. They were at least really friends with Amami, supposedly.

Also, when Maki found Umi alone in a classroom after she left the roof, she cried but didn't cry aloud and kept talking with him. I thought she might've cried a lot as characters in other anime often do, but she didn't, and that was good, and more genuine. Moreover, she still cared about Amami at that time, so she really was kind to her.

I wondered why Amami asked those 2 things of Umi and Maki, but then I think she wanted Maki to be the one who never left Umi, perhaps? Maybe she also had a complex feeling at that time because she wanted to be the best friend of Umi. I didn't fully understand what she was trying to do when she was playing a ghost, but maybe she wanted to see how Umi talked with him and wanted to feel the difference, and just got her head around it.

Umi showed her more decisiveness and initiative than Maki at the end of this episode. He wasn't familiar with being around people, so he wasn't very brave, and the episode showed these things well even at the end. And she also still was a little playful. Anyhow, overall, episode 5 wrapped up one arc of the plot so far. Maybe this was the first volume of the original light novel, I guess. It was a clean, well-organized, convincing story that brought the characters to life.

For animations, I felt like when Umi and Amami were at the 3rd year grade, their heads were too big as a character design. Then when they became 1st years in middle school, they were almost identical to how they look in high school. Also, Umi's eye color is red, and nothing was said about it, though the color of Amami's eyes was mentioned and some kids stayed away from Amami because of her eye color. Which one is weirder. Well, that's anime world.

What's going to come? Well, I was glad that Amami also started liking Maki like regular rom-coms do, but it seemed that she cared about him because she perhaps started noticing that Umi was hanging out with him. So, that won't come, I suppose. But there will be rumors about Umi and Maki because they walked around the school during the festival, so probably more people will talk about them and start a new story. If it's an ordinary rom-com anime, then another person who falls in love with Umi or Maki will appear and a few of them will start doing something. Amami definitely had the position, but it seemed she didn't play that role, so I guessed there would be a new guy who got along with them from the next episode.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 4
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the First Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 4. 7/10.

  • Story and characters: 4/5
  • Animation: 3/5
  • BGM: 3/5

The earlier part of this episode was that Amami asked a question which is hard to say publicly to other classmates, and then Asanagi pretended to have won in a drawing for the member of a school festival committee. The later part was its preparation and the festival itself.

The festival was pretty short in the anime, and rather, the story focused on the relationship between Amami and Asanagi. Amami at last found out Asanagi became friends with Maehara, but she didn't say why before the festival, and then at the end of this episode, after the festival, she finally made up her mind to talk to her.

From the story's point of view, it was 4/5. Well, finally, it was good plot that the story wasn't from the main heroine who can do anything like Amami. I felt a little of how Asanagi felt to Amami, but because Amami can do anything even what Asanagi wanted, and Asanagi didn't say anything bad to Amami, her inferiority complex toward Amami got bigger. There was a character having some inferiority complex for sure, but maybe for her, that's almost everything due to Amami. Because of that, she was kinda attractive character as she is more complicated and not too fictional character. Also, she didn't want to have a bad relationship with Amami because she still thinks Amami is the best friend, or at least that's what I felt. When Asanagi and Maehara talked about themselves and he didn't ask what happened to them, that was kinda unexpected. But it shows his character well as he didn't have a good friendship relationship and wanted to protect one's personal issue to themselves unless they want to. The festival itself was surprisingly quick and I didn't expect that much, but it was just for an art exhibition so it kinda makes sense.

In terms of animation and BGMs, I didn't feel anything so they were 3/5. The mosaic art of empty cans was unexpectedly big and really good, though. It was as high as 2 or 3 floors of the school building, with a complicated character design.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 3
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the First Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 3. 7/10. Well, Asanagi for sure can be the prettiest in the class, and also Maehara became friends with Amami and the story moved forward through her actions too.

The earlier part of this episode was, first, that Amami invited Maehara to lunch at school — alone at first, and then with Asanagi too — and second, that they went to Maehara's home. She talked loudly in class without caring about other people, as she always does, and that characteristic didn't match Maehara's personality. But he was alone before he met Asanagi in his class, so I guess he had mixed feelings toward her. Anyhow, she was kind enough to take his word seriously and tried not to invite many people to the lunch. It was good animation to see that Asanagi apologized by putting her hands together with her mobile phone, from a distance. I've never seen anything like this.

At the lunch, Maehara showed his great cooking skill. Somehow, characters like him have great cooking skills and help with their parents' work, not only in this anime, and he was way better than Amami and she lost her confidence. I wondered why Amami talked to him often, and what she said was he was nice and had his own opinions. Well, I thought it felt shallow, but maybe she was a girl who didn't hear any different opinions from others because everyone except her friends just flirts with her.

Because his cooking skill was good, they went to his house, and had a few things to eat. And she was unexpectedly good at playing games, so much that she even taught him how to play. Well, I guess this character is basically good at almost anything, more than other people, so she's just a capable person? But having an ability has nothing to do with being the prettiest, I guess, so this was how the author wanted her to be.

Then, while they were heading back, he turned down a phone call from Amami, saying he couldn't hang out with her because there was another one. I wasn't sure how Asanagi felt, but maybe Asanagi thought anyone would give priority to Amami over her. Or she wasn't confident about it. Then after hearing that he turned down, she went back to his home and just said a few words at the door of his house. From his perspective, it didn't make sense at all. So she couldn't stop her feelings and ran to his house to say something directly. It was cute.

The later half of this episode was about, first, Asanagi hanging out with him and sleeping over at his house, and second, them visiting her house.

Asanagi was so relaxed with him and they liked the same things, and they started reading the final volume of a manga at the same time, sitting close together. Then they fell asleep in his bed, and he slept in an awkward position. Well, obviously she was too relaxed, let her guard down, and they were dating already. Then after they woke up, instead of sending her home they slept over in the house with his mother. Where was his father? Was there any reason his father wasn't there? Anyhow, she borrowed his sweats and slept in a bed and finally talked about telling Amami about their relationship when there was a good chance. I guess Amami would find out about it beforehand and there would be trouble.

Then, because of that, they visited her home next so he was able to apologize. Her mother was there and wanted to ask him about the details of what happened between them. It was, well, interesting to her mother for sure, and no wonder that she also didn't want to tell her mother about them. So, she was also kinda a person who keeps things to herself. As expected, he was the first boyfriend of hers that her mother had met.

Lastly, in a classroom, a teacher tried to decide the members of the school festival committee and nobody volunteered. It was a little bit weird that neither Amami nor Asanagi volunteered. And then, Maehara was nominated, obviously. But then some classmates badmouthed him. So it seems he's mentally strong so he can somehow put up with being alone, but not strong enough to take that kind of thing. Well, most people wouldn't be. Asanagi quietly got mad, and then Amami was trying to question that badmouthing in front of the whole class.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 2
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 2.

The episode started when a guy asked Asanagi out, and she turned him down and then he asked to exchange contact information but she also turned it down. That guy also tried the same thing with Amami, so they thought he was flirty. Then Amami and another girl tried to leave that place, but before leaving, somehow, Amami got Maehara's phone number. I was like, what? Why? Did they want to talk about Asanagi turning a guy down?

Anyhow, Maehara talked with Asanagi about the scene they had seen, when they played together in his house. She didn't care, and they also started talking about what being popular is like. She was popular, but he didn't want it because it got attention from others and you needed to care too much about other people. She thought he was a dweeb, and well, I kinda agreed with her, but apparently, he was right after watching the later part of this episode, because Asanagi was exactly the type of person he talked about. Anyway, they started playing games as usual. And surprisingly, that day was not the day they had talked about going out in the previous episode.

Then they went out together on Friday after school. Instead of going places together, they met up at the place, and they also changed their clothes from their school uniforms to their own clothes. Asanagi wore a short sleeve hoodie and jeans and Maehara wore a black shirt with the word "Destroy" on it and pants, and she said to him that it was too black and it stood out. She wanted to make him more fashionable next time, and that made him happy because it meant there would be a next time. Well, but he should've thought what kinds of clothes he would wear, I guess, because he probably wasn't used to it. He also told her it was bad that she had to cancel hanging out with her friends like Amami, and she said it was okay because she still did that on days other than Friday. But it was obviously a lie because they hung out together before when she turned down a guy's confession.

Anyway, they at first went to anime goods stores and it was new for her and she was interested but he didn't want to show it to her because, well, probably it wasn't something normal people were into. Then they went to have hamburgers but then the students from the same school saw them there and recognized her. So they started acting like a couple, which made the students misunderstand and think she wasn't Asanagi, because they couldn't believe Asanagi would be dating Maehara. But because they didn't like the gossip, they went to an arcade and played games. As usual, they had a lot of money for high school students. While Asanagi went to the restroom and Maehara waited on a bench, he happened to run into Amami and other 4 classmates. Then he suddenly called Asanagi, and I wasn't sure what he was trying to do, but it made sense that he wanted to let her know that Amami was there. Then he was trying to leave the place with his friend's bag. Well, he was supposed to be waiting for his friend, but he tried to leave before his friend even came back, so it must have looked to Amami like he was leaving because of her. Anyway, then Amami suggested hanging out together, and Maehara knew that Asanagi didn't want to meet them, so he was trying to turn her down. But she was stubborn and he learned that Asanagi sometimes wanted to stay away from her because she wanted to spend her own time, I guess. So he spoke plainly, said he didn't want to hang out with many people, and left. Asanagi caught up with him and thanked him.

And then, they took a train and went back to their homes and he was tired and went to sleep. But this was confusing to me. Taking trains, and a distance long enough for him to fall asleep, means they went far from home. But they met with a few classmates or students from the same school, so it should have been close enough. And also they changed clothes after school, so the places should have been close enough for that. So, this taking trains scenes felt weird. Maybe I'm overthinking it, and they just hung out together and went too far from their homes instead of hanging out in a small area, though.

Anyhow, then the other day, Amami apologized to him in a class while everyone listened, and she let slip that she had his phone number which she should've kept a secret. Every classmate got jealous and he had butterflies in his stomach. After a class, Amami, Asanagi and Maehara went back from a school together. Why Asanagi? No idea. Probably she insisted coming together. And why not another girl? No idea. Asanagi also pretended that she didn't hang out with Maehara often. So she was trying to follow them and he suggested going to his home. At his home, Amami wanted to apologize and then Maehara talked to Amami about something. I forgot what it was. Probably he was more comfortable being alone and there was some types of people like that to her. Then she agreed with him and complimented him, saying he was very kind to his friend, well, Asanagi. And she also heard it and blushed at it, so she suggested leaving his home with Amami.

So, in this episode, some scenes felt odd or had strange setups, but that's for the sake of the story the author wanted to write, so it was still good. And this slice-of-life anime is a little bit different from others in terms of rom-com, especially Asanagi and Maehara's relationship so far, so that part is also good. They also have something in common: they both love sharks, and sharks with angel wings.

item.title: First thoughts after watching I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class Episode 1
item.description:
This note includes a spoiler.

I watched I Made Friends with the Second Prettiest Girl in My Class episode 1.

The main character was a typical guy in a slice-of-life anime, who didn't have any friends and was an introvert and enjoyed being alone. I don't even remember his name lol. And he liked some movies or Netflix that other people didn't watch. At his high school, he needed to introduce himself at first, and he couldn't introduce himself like a sociable person does. And then, the next person was the one who was supposed to be the prettiest girl in the classroom, I guess, and while she introduced herself, she also introduced Asanagi, the main heroine, obviously. The character design, or maybe drawing, made me feel sometimes that her body or her shoulders were really wide for some reason at first, and it felt a little bit weird. It was gone shortly, though. That girl reacted a little bit when she heard that he spent the weekend at home watching movies or playing video games. Like other slice-of-life anime, other guys who cared about looks talked about how hot their classmates were. But then, I couldn't imagine how the MC and MH got familiar with each other. And also, the main character wasn't really appealing at that time to me, as he was maybe a little depressing.

Then as the days went by, he didn't join any activity after school, and went back to a Blu-ray shop for movies. And then he met Asanagi, and she actually wanted to talk to him and decided not to spend time with her friends. The main character also knew she liked movies or TV shows and they talked about them, and they knew and liked similar things.

Soon after, they started spending time at his house and played games while eating pizza. Their pizza tastes were also alike and what he ordered was exactly what she liked. But how she played a game was different, and she couldn't win against him, so maybe she didn't play video games a lot. For some reason, in his room, there was a couch, but they sat on the floor and played video games there, and that felt really weird to me. Anyhow, while I was watching, they were already a match made in heaven. That was the 3rd day they met, and they decided to meet up outside next time.

The next scene was not a date scene on that day. It was at school, and he ate his boxed lunch by himself outside, like always, alone. But then he came across someone trying to confess to her and he wanted to leave the place, but then her friends came, and the episode ended.

Well, not that bad an episode, and the character designs, drawings, and animation are bright, shiny, and cute overall. The plot was at first a little bit typical, but it seemed good, too, and maybe it's going to be fun for later episodes.
